claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi HEA is coarse-grained.
Unreinforced CoCrFeNi exhibits an increasing coefficient of friction over a broad sliding-temperature range.
Unreinforced CoCrFeNi exhibits variable or accelerated wear as temperature, load, or environment changes.
Approximately 0.6 wt% graphene oxide can be incorporated into an HEA through mechanical alloying and spark-plasma sintering to produce a composite.
Dispersed graphene in the CoCrFeNi matrix will cause grain refinement.
Graphene reinforcement will form a continuous or semi-continuous carbonaceous transfer layer at the sliding interface.
Graphene basal planes will undergo shear slip during sliding.
Basal-plane shear and the resulting transfer film will reduce interfacial shear stress.
Graphene-induced microstructural refinement will produce grain-boundary strengthening.
Grain-boundary strengthening will delay wear-related damage and stabilize tribological behavior over wide temperature and load ranges.
Graphene-reinforced CoCrFeNi will have a markedly lower coefficient of friction than unreinforced CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
Graphene-reinforced CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than unreinforced CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
The graphene-derived film will mitigate the usual increase in friction at intermediate temperatures.
The intervention will remain effective in dry or controlled atmospheres up to 800 °C under moderate-to-high loads.
Aggressive oxidizing atmospheres may oxidize graphene and compromise its lubricating effect.
Extreme loads may overwhelm the lubricating effect of graphene.
Graphene oxidation stability and long-term retention at the sliding interface near 800 °C are uncertain.

A controlled comparison will use unreinforced and approximately 0.6 wt% graphene-oxide-reinforced CoCrFeNi samples consolidated identically and tested by ball-on-disk sliding from room temperature to 800 °C under identical loads.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if the reinforced samples fail to show significantly lower friction and wear over the majority of the temperature range and no uniform carbonaceous film is observed.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims maintained improvement throughout the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range, but the falsification rule only requires failure across a majority of that range and also requires absence of a film. It could therefore fail at some temperatures, or fail tribologically despite film formation, without meeting the stated falsification criterion.
